notes: §1985:VII.2.3.4 GR4 says the ACCESS MODE, FILE STATUS, ORGANIZATION IS SEQUENTIAL, PADDING CHARACTER, RECORD DELIMITER and RESERVE clauses "are presented in alphabetical order on the following pages": a statement of where the standard prints the six clauses, with no requirement on a program or on the object program (the order of the clauses in source is §1985:VII.2.3.3 SR1's: "The clauses which follow the SELECT clause may appear in any order."). What the compiler owes the rule is that each clause it names is a clause of the sequential file control entry at 85: each is an alternative of fileControlClauses; BindFileControl reads five of them, and PADDING CHARACTER is parsed and kept nowhere, its one reader being the edition arm VisitPaddingCharacterClause (accepted at 85, obsolete at 2002, refused from 2014); none has a gate that refuses it at --std 85. Probed at 85: one sequential entry writing all six, in the rule's alphabetical order and with ASSIGN last, compiles and runs (RECORD DELIMITER IS STANDARD-1 with the warning COBOL1778 that the clause has no effect, the others silently). The rules of each clause are their own rows (the PADDING CHARACTER operand rules are kb/Work PB5070). The witness writes FILE STATUS, ORGANIZATION and ACCESS MODE in that order on one entry and reads back a record and status 00.

next.reason: 1985 GR4 only says the ACCESS MODE, FILE STATUS, ORGANIZATION, PADDING CHARACTER, RECORD DELIMITER and RESERVE clauses 'are presented in alphabetical order on the following pages': a note on the document's layout, with no requirement on a program or implementation. 2023 has no rule stating presentation order (the word 'alphabetical' does not occur in specs/ISO_COBOL_2023.md), and its file control clauses are each a subclause of §2023:12.4.5. No rule carries it; no program's meaning depends on it.
